examples: The ceremony will commence at exactly nine o'clock, so guests should arrive early.
این مراسم ساعت نه دقیقاً آغاز خواهد شد، پس مهمانان باید زود برسند.
Before the trial could commence, the judge asked both lawyers to confirm they were ready.
پیش از آنکه محاکمه آغاز شود، قاضی از هر دو وکیل خواست تأیید کنند که آماده‌اند.
Construction work is set to commence next spring once the permits are approved.
کار ساخت‌وساز قرار است بهار آینده، پس از تأیید مجوزها، آغاز شود.
miniContext: At a formal event such as a graduation or a trial, people often use the word commence instead of simply saying 'start,' because it sounds more official. The ceremony will commence once all the guests have taken their seats, and no one is allowed to leave before it ends. Lawyers, judges, and officials prefer this word in written announcements and speeches. Hearing commence usually signals that something important and carefully planned is about to begin.

examples: Every autumn, thousands of birds migrate south to escape the cold winter.
هر پاییز، هزاران پرنده به سمت جنوب مهاجرت می‌کنند تا از سرمای زمستان دوری کنند.
Many young people migrate to big cities in search of better job opportunities.
بسیاری از جوانان برای یافتن فرصت‌های شغلی بهتر به شهرهای بزرگ مهاجرت می‌کنند.
Scientists tracked how the whales migrated across the ocean using satellite tags.
دانشمندان با استفاده از ردیاب‌های ماهواره‌ای مهاجرت نهنگ‌ها را در سراسر اقیانوس دنبال کردند.
miniContext: Each year, certain animals migrate over long distances to find food, warmer weather, or a safe place to breed. Geese migrate in large flocks, flying in a V-shaped pattern that helps them conserve energy. Humans migrate too, often leaving their home country to study, work, or escape conflict. Whether it's birds crossing continents or families moving abroad, the word migrate always describes this kind of purposeful journey from one place to another.

examples: The polished silver trophy began to gleam under the bright stage lights.
جام نقره‌ای صیقل‌خورده زیر نورهای درخشان صحنه شروع به درخشیدن کرد.
Her eyes seemed to gleam with excitement when she heard the good news.
وقتی خبر خوب را شنید، چشمانش از ذوق برق زد.
After we waxed the car, its surface gleamed like new in the sunlight.
بعد از اینکه ماشین را واکس زدیم، سطح آن زیر نور خورشید مثل نو می‌درخشید.
miniContext: A clean window, a polished shoe, or a drop of dew can all gleam when light hits them just right. The word describes a brief, bright flash of light rather than a steady glow. Writers often use gleam to add a sense of beauty or hope to a scene, such as a distant light that seems to gleam on the horizon. You can also say someone's eyes gleam with mischief or joy, giving the word an emotional meaning as well as a visual one.

examples: The severe famine forced thousands of families to leave their farms and search for food elsewhere.
قحطی شدید هزاران خانواده را مجبور کرد مزارع خود را ترک کنند و در جایی دیگر به دنبال غذا بگردند.
Years of drought eventually led to a widespread famine across the region.
سال‌ها خشکسالی سرانجام به قحطی گسترده‌ای در آن منطقه منجر شد.
Historians still study the causes of the famine that struck Ireland in the nineteenth century.
تاریخ‌نگاران هنوز علل قحطی‌ای را که در قرن نوزدهم ایرلند را درگیر کرد بررسی می‌کنند.
miniContext: A famine occurs when a lack of food affects a large population for an extended period, often because of drought, war, or crop failure. During a famine, prices for basic food rise sharply, and many people depend on aid from other countries to survive. Governments and charities often respond to a famine by sending emergency supplies of grain, water, and medicine. Throughout history, a famine has sometimes changed the course of nations, driving mass migration and political upheaval.

examples: The cargo vessel carried containers full of electronics across the Pacific Ocean.
کشتی باربری، کانتینرهایی پر از وسایل الکترونیکی را در سراسر اقیانوس آرام حمل می‌کرد.
Pour the hot soup into a heatproof vessel before serving it to the guests.
سوپ داغ را پیش از سرو به مهمانان داخل یک ظرف مقاوم در برابر گرما بریزید.
The ancient vessel discovered by divers had been resting on the seabed for centuries.
ظرف باستانی‌ای که غواصان پیدا کردند قرن‌ها روی بستر دریا باقی مانده بود.
miniContext: A vessel can be a large ship used for carrying passengers or cargo across water, or it can be a smaller container used for holding liquids. Sailors refer to any boat, from a fishing vessel to a naval destroyer, using this word. In a kitchen or a laboratory, a glass or metal vessel might hold anything from soup to chemicals. Because the word covers both meanings, context usually makes clear whether a vessel is meant to sail the sea or simply sit on a shelf.

examples: Police asked witnesses to identify the suspect from a lineup of photographs.
پلیس از شاهدان خواست مظنون را از میان مجموعه‌ای از عکس‌ها شناسایی کنند.
Doctors ran several tests to identify the exact cause of her persistent headaches.
پزشکان چند آزمایش انجام دادند تا علت دقیق سردردهای مداوم او را شناسایی کنند.
Students learned to identify different types of rocks by examining their color and texture.
دانش‌آموزان یاد گرفتند انواع مختلف سنگ‌ها را با بررسی رنگ و بافت آن‌ها شناسایی کنند.
miniContext: To identify something means to recognize exactly what it is or who it is, often by comparing details against known information. A detective might identify a criminal using fingerprints, while a botanist might identify a plant by its leaves and flowers. Schools teach students to identify patterns in math or grammar so they can apply the same logic elsewhere. Being able to identify a problem correctly is usually the first step toward solving it.

examples: An observant shopper quickly noticed that the price tag didn't match the receipt.
یک خریدار دقیق و نکته‌سنج سریعاً متوجه شد که برچسب قیمت با رسید مطابقت ندارد.
Good detectives tend to be extremely observant, noticing small details that others overlook.
کارآگاهان خوب معمولاً بسیار دقیق و نکته‌سنج هستند و جزئیات کوچکی را که دیگران نادیده می‌گیرند متوجه می‌شوند.
Her observant nature helped her realize that something was wrong before anyone else did.
خاصیت دقیق و نکته‌سنج او باعث شد پیش از هر کس دیگری متوجه شود که چیزی اشتباه است.
miniContext: An observant person pays close attention to their surroundings and notices small details that most people miss. Teachers appreciate observant students who catch mistakes on the board before being told, and parents often rely on an observant babysitter to spot a child's mood changes. Being observant isn't just about having good eyesight; it also means thinking carefully about what you see. In many jobs, from security guard to scientist, being observant can make the difference between success and failure.

examples: The editor spent hours correcting grammar mistakes before approving the final draft.
ویراستار ساعت‌ها صرف اصلاح اشتباهات گرامری کرد پیش از آنکه نسخه نهایی را تأیید کند.
She sent her manuscript to an editor who suggested cutting the first three chapters.
او دست‌نوشته‌اش را برای یک ویراستار فرستاد که پیشنهاد داد سه فصل اول حذف شود.
As the newspaper's chief editor, he decides which stories appear on the front page.
او به‌عنوان سردبیر روزنامه تصمیم می‌گیرد کدام داستان‌ها در صفحه اول چاپ شوند.
miniContext: An editor reviews written work, checking it for grammar, clarity, and overall quality before it gets published. In a newsroom, an editor decides which stories are worth printing and how they should be written. Book publishers rely on an editor to shape a messy first draft into a polished, readable novel. Working closely with an editor can be humbling for a writer, since even a carefully written piece almost always needs changes.

examples: Paramedics worked quickly to revive the man after his heart stopped beating.
پرسنل اورژانس به سرعت کار کردند تا مرد را پس از توقف ضربان قلبش احیا کنند.
The company hoped a new marketing campaign would revive sales after a slow year.
شرکت امید داشت که یک کمپین تبلیغاتی جدید فروش را پس از یک سال ضعیف احیا کند.
Watering the wilted plant every day eventually revived it.
آبیاری روزانه آن گیاه پرپرشده سرانجام آن را احیا کرد.
miniContext: To revive someone or something means to bring it back to life, energy, or health after a period of weakness or decline. Doctors try to revive patients whose hearts have stopped using CPR or electric shocks. A struggling business might revive its fortunes by launching an exciting new product, and a tired traveler can revive their energy with a strong cup of coffee. Whether applied to people, plants, or economies, revive always carries the sense of restoring something that had nearly been lost.

examples: Even after several rejections, she decided to persist with her plan to open a bakery.
حتی پس از چند بار رد شدن، او تصمیم گرفت در برنامه‌اش برای راه‌اندازی یک نان‌وایی پافشاری کند.
If the pain in your knee persists for more than a week, you should see a doctor.
اگر درد زانوی شما بیش از یک هفته ادامه پیدا کند، باید به پزشک مراجعه کنید.
Despite the heavy criticism, the researchers persisted with their experiment until they found an answer.
علی‌رغم انتقادات شدید، محققان با آزمایش خود پافشاری کردند تا سرانجام پاسخی پیدا کردند.
miniContext: To persist means to continue doing something or to keep existing, even when faced with difficulty or opposition. A determined athlete will persist through injuries and setbacks to reach a goal, while a stubborn rumor might persist for years despite being proven false. Doctors often warn patients that if symptoms persist, further testing may be necessary. Persisting through hardship is frequently what separates people who eventually succeed from those who give up too soon.

examples: The mountains looked hazy in the distance because of the morning fog.
کوه‌ها به‌خاطر مه صبحگاهی در دوردست مه‌آلود به نظر می‌رسیدند.
My memory of that night is hazy, so I can't recall exactly what happened.
خاطره‌ام از آن شب مبهم است، پس نمی‌توانم دقیقاً به یاد بیاورم چه اتفاقی افتاد.
On hazy summer afternoons, the sun turns a dull orange color behind the smoke.
در بعدازظهرهای مه‌آلود تابستانی، خورشید پشت دود به رنگ نارنجی کم‌رنگی درمی‌آید.
miniContext: Something hazy is unclear or hard to see distinctly, whether because of fog, smoke, dust, or simply fading memory. On a hazy day, distant buildings and hills seem to blur into a soft gray outline. People also describe their thinking or memories as hazy when details feel vague or difficult to pin down, such as a hazy recollection of a dream. The word captures a gentle kind of uncertainty, somewhere between clearly visible and completely hidden.

examples: The journalist interviewed several witnesses before writing her report on the accident.
روزنامه‌نگار پیش از نوشتن گزارش خود دربارهٔ تصادف، با چند شاهد مصاحبه کرد.
A good journalist always checks facts carefully before publishing a story.
یک روزنامه‌نگار خوب همیشه پیش از انتشار یک خبر، واقعیت‌ها را با دقت بررسی می‌کند.
He worked as a journalist for a local newspaper for nearly twenty years.
او نزدیک به بیست سال به‌عنوان روزنامه‌نگار برای یک روزنامهٔ محلی کار کرد.
miniContext: A journalist gathers information, investigates events, and writes or broadcasts news stories for the public. Some journalists specialize in dangerous assignments, traveling to war zones to report firsthand, while others cover local politics or sports for a small-town paper. A skilled journalist knows how to ask the right questions and present facts clearly and fairly. Freedom of the press depends heavily on journalists who are willing to hold powerful people accountable.
